lines: Quantizer that builds its set of target pitches from a reference melody it has heard, weighting them by how often each pitch occurs rather than following a chosen scale
Turns off the statistical weighting and quantizes chromatically, to twelve-tone equal temperament
Stops new reference events being written into the data table; quantizing carries on from what is already stored, and those stored events are saved with the patch
Holds the output pitch until the next rising edge at the GATE input, so the pitch does not jump when the reference changes; it applies to the CHORD output as well
Erases every pitch event in the data table and turns FREEZE off
Three settings: LAST weighs the most recent pitch interval at the CV input, MOST weighs the most frequent interval in the active region, and OFF weighs neither
Sets where the active region of the data table starts, counted in events back from the newest, so quantizing can follow earlier pitches; a red light comes on when that region is empty
Biases the weighting towards high pitches turned clockwise and low pitches turned anticlockwise, five times the weight at one end against a fifth at the other; centred it applies no bias
Biases the weighting towards pitches held for long gates turned clockwise and short gates turned anticlockwise, five times the weight against a fifth; centred it applies no bias
Sets how many notes the CHORD output carries, 1 to 5, taking the highest weighted pitches
Sets how many target pitches incoming notes are quantized to, 1 to 12; at 1 only one pitch ever comes out, and at 12 the module quantizes chromatically
Sets how many of the stored reference events are used to work out the weighting, 4 to 240; low values follow the reference closely, high values smooth it out
A trigger here toggles THRU
A trigger here toggles FREEZE
A trigger here clears the data table and turns FREEZE off
Added to the PITCHES knob, at 1.1 pitches per volt
Added to the PERSIST knob; 10V adds the full 240 events
Added to the OFFSET knob; 10V adds the full 240 events
Added to the OCTAVE knob; 5V covers its whole range
Added to the DURATION knob; 5V covers its whole range
The monophonic pitch to be quantized
Gate for the pitch being quantized; it marks each note event and triggers the sample and hold
Pitch of the reference performance, recorded into the data table
Gate for the reference pitch; each rising edge stores one event with its pitch, octave, duration and interval
Polyphonic pitch output carrying the highest weighted target pitches, as many of them as CHORD is set to
The quantized pitch
A copy of the gate at the GATE input
Note — the warning light beside the module name comes on when the active region of the data table is empty, and when all twelve notes are in use
Menu — reset of data table chooses what RESET does: clear it all, clear it and prime it with the four most recent reference events, or leave it alone and only release FREEZE
Menu — skip repeats of same ref note stores a run of identical reference pitches as a single event
Six-channel trigger sequencer of 64 steps played in from one big button; it runs whenever its clock runs and has no run control of its own
Punches a trigger into the current step of the current channel; pressing it on a step that already has one changes nothing
A trigger here punches a trigger into the current step of the current channel
Advances the sequencer one step per pulse; stopping this clock is the only way to stop the sequencer
Chooses which of the six channels every button acts on; it can be turned while the sequencer runs and takes effect at once
Chooses the channel from a voltage, 0-10V spread over the six channels
Sets the chance that the trigger of the step about to be reached is flipped in the current channel: at the left end nothing changes, at the right end every step is flipped, which inverts the pattern
Added to the RND knob after being divided by ten, so 10V reaches full probability with the knob at its left end
Sets how many steps the current channel plays before it loops round, 1 to 64
Added to the LEN knob, 10V covering the whole 64 steps
Switches the current channel between its two stored sequences
A trigger here switches the current channel between its two stored sequences
Clears every trigger of the current channel while it is held down
Above 0.5V here clears every trigger of the current channel, for as long as the voltage stays high
Clears the trigger at the current step while it is held down, so holding it through several steps clears them all
Above 0.5V here clears the trigger at the current step, and goes on clearing each step while it stays high
Plays a trigger on every clock pulse of the current channel while it is held down, starting on the next pulse
Above 0.5V here plays a trigger on every clock pulse of the current channel while it stays high
With this off, the triggers played by FILL sound but are not written into the sequence
Returns every channel to its first step
A trigger here returns every channel to its first step
Quantizes the big button and DEL to the nearest beat rather than the beat last reached; it needs a steady clock of at least 30 BPM, and switches itself off internally below that
A 1ms trigger on each step of that channel that holds one
Menu — Big and Del on next step registers every big button and DEL press on the step after the current one, and SNAP then has no effect
Six-channel gate and CV sequencer of 128 steps played in from one big button; it runs whenever its clock runs and has no run control of its own
Turns on the gate of the current step in the current channel and stores the voltage at CV IN as that step's CV
A trigger here turns on the gate of the current step and stores the voltage at CV IN as that step's CV
Advances the sequencer one step per pulse; stopping this clock is the only way to stop the sequencer
Advances the sequencer one step for each press, for programming a sequence without a running clock
Chooses which of the six channels every button acts on; it can be turned while the sequencer runs and takes effect at once
Chooses the channel from a voltage, 0-10V spread over the six channels
Sets the chance that the gate of the step about to be reached is flipped in the current channel: at the left end nothing changes, at the right end every step is flipped
Added to the RND knob after being divided by ten, so 10V reaches full probability with the knob at its left end
Sets how many steps the current channel plays before it loops round, 1 to 128
Added to the LEN knob, 10V covering the whole 128 steps
Switches the display between the length of the current channel and the step it has reached
Switches the current channel between its two stored sequences
A trigger here switches the current channel between its two stored sequences
Clears the gate at the current step while it is held down, so holding it through several steps clears them all
Above 0.5V here clears the gate at the current step, and goes on clearing each step while it stays high
Turns off every gate of the current channel and returns all of its stored voltages to C4
A trigger here turns off every gate of the current channel and returns all of its stored voltages to C4
Plays a gate on every clock pulse of the current channel while it is held down, starting on the next pulse
Above 0.5V here plays a gate on every clock pulse of the current channel while it stays high
With this off, the gates played by FILL sound but are not written into the sequence
The voltage taken into a step when the big button is pressed, and taken on every clock pulse while FILL runs with MEM on, which is how the module is used as a CV recorder
Returns every channel to its first step
A trigger here returns every channel to its first step
Quantizes the big button and DEL to the nearest beat rather than the beat last reached; it needs a steady clock of at least 30 BPM, and switches itself off internally below that
Samples each channel's CV output on that channel's own gate, so the voltage changes only as a gate fires
The clock pulse itself on each step of that channel that holds a gate
The stored voltage of the step that channel has reached
Keyboard chord generator holding 25 chords of up to four notes each, recalled by index; the CHD-X expander adds four quantizers that snap pitches to the active chord
Transposes the chord down one semitone, moving the octave values to match
Transposes the chord up one semitone, moving the octave values to match
Steps the octave of that note of the chord down; the range runs from a dash through 0 to 9, and the dash takes that note out of the chord
Steps the octave of that note of the chord up; the range runs from a dash through 0 to 9, and the dash takes that note out of the chord
Selects which of the 25 stored chords is active
Overrides the GATE input and holds every gate output at 10V, so the chord sounds while it is being set up
Added to the INDEX knob to pick the chord, a semitone per chord: 0V is the first chord and 2V the twenty-fifth, matching the notes C4 to C6
A monophonic gate here fires the gate output of every active note at once; with a polyphonic gate, channel N drives the Nth note of the chord, which can be used to arpeggiate it
Pitch of that note of the chord
Gate for that note of the chord, taken from the GATE input or forced on by FORCE
Note — a key press sets one of the four notes of the chord, chosen by how far down the key it lands; the key is split into four bands, the top band setting the first note
Menu — keypress monitoring sounds the whole chord while a key is held with the left mouse button, and only the note pressed with the right button
Menu — poly merge outputs into top note folds the second row, the second and third, or all three lower rows into the top row, whose CV and gate outputs then become polyphonic
Menu — copy chord and paste chord move a chord between index positions through an internal memory, keeping unused notes in place
Menu — portable sequence copies the chord out for other modules, either as one step holding the chord or arpeggiated across four steps, and pastes one back either way
Expander for Chord-Key, placed immediately to the right of it: four quantizers that snap incoming pitches to the notes of the chord selected in Chord-Key. On its own it quantizes chromatically
Pitch to be quantized on that channel; a polyphonic cable is quantized channel by channel
Transposes that channel by whole octaves, -4 to +4, before it is quantized
The quantized pitch for that channel
Master clock with three sub-clocks, each running at its own ratio of the master tempo; it can be chained with other clocks and locked to an external clock source
Sets the master tempo in whole BPM, 30 to 300
Restarts the time keeping of the master clock and of all three sub-clocks
Pause and play. The outputs hold their state while it is off, and the clock resumes where it stopped, so sub-clocks at different ratios stay in step
Steps back through the tempo modes, which are BPM CV and external sync at 24, 16, 12, 8, 4 or 2 pulses per step
Steps forward through the tempo modes, which are BPM CV and external sync at 2, 4, 8, 12, 16 or 24 pulses per step
Swing on the master clock, -99 to +99: every even pulse is moved earlier or later while the odd pulses hold their place, and at centre the pulses are evenly spaced
Duration of the master clock pulse. The pulse and the gap after it are each held to at least 1ms whatever the swing setting
Ratio of that clock to the master tempo: turned up it multiplies, turned down it divides, through every whole number to 16 plus 1.5 and 2.5, then selected values on to 96
Swing on that sub-clock, -99 to +99: every even pulse of that clock is moved earlier or later while the odd pulses hold their place
Duration of that sub-clock's pulse. The pulse and the gap after it are each held to at least 1ms
Delays that sub-clock against the master by a fraction of its own clock period: none, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3 or 3/4
A trigger here restarts the time keeping of the master clock and all three sub-clocks
A trigger here toggles between run and pause; the menu can make this input follow a gate level instead

In CV mode this sets the tempo, with 0V giving 120 BPM and each volt doubling it. In a sync mode the clock locks to the pulses arriving here, and with nothing patched the tempo comes from the BPM knob
The master clock pulse, at the tempo shown on the BPM display
The pulse of that sub-clock, at its own ratio of the master tempo
A 10V pulse when the module is reset, for passing the reset on to sequencers or to another clock
A 10V pulse when run is switched on or off, for passing the run state on to sequencers or to another clock
Passes on the voltage at the BPM input when a cable is patched there; with nothing patched it gives the module's own tempo as a BPM CV
Menu — Outputs high on reset when not running holds the clock outputs high while a stopped clock is reset, so a sequential switch reset at that moment is not stepped on
Menu — On Start and On Stop each offer an internal reset and a reset pulse, so the clock and the sequencers it drives restart together
Menu — Display delay values in notes shows the delay settings as note lengths instead of clock fractions, one quarter note being one clock period
Menu — Run CV input is level sensitive makes the RUN input follow a gate rather than a trigger; in a chain of clocks only the first should have it turned on
Menu — Auto-patch makes this the clock master and patches the reset, run and BPM inputs of the other Clocked and Clkd modules to it, leaving already-patched inputs alone
Menu — Add expander places the 4HP expander that adds pulse width and swing CV inputs
Expander for Clocked, 4HP, placed immediately to the right of it; it adds CV inputs for the pulse width and swing settings of the master clock and the three sub-clocks
Modulates the pulse width of the master clock on Clocked, -5V to 5V with that PW knob at its default; with the knob full left the range is 0V to 10V, 5V giving the normal width
Modulates the pulse width of that sub-clock on Clocked, -5V to 5V with that PW knob at its default; with the knob full left the range is 0V to 10V, 5V giving the normal width
Modulates the swing of the master clock on Clocked. With that SWING knob at its default the range is -5V to 5V; with the knob turned full left the range becomes 0V to 10V, where 5V gives no swing
Modulates the swing of that sub-clock on Clocked. With that SWING knob at its default the range is -5V to 5V; with the knob turned full left the range becomes 0V to 10V, where 5V gives no swing
Master clock with three sub-clocks, each running at its own ratio of the master tempo; it can be chained with other clocks and locked to an external clock source
Restarts the time keeping of the master clock and of all three sub-clocks
Pause and play. The outputs hold their state while it is off, and the clock resumes where it stopped, so sub-clocks at different ratios stay in step
Sets the master tempo in whole BPM, 30 to 300
Steps the display back through the four values it can show: the master tempo, then the ratio of each of the three sub-clocks
Steps the display forward through the four values it can show: the master tempo, then the ratio of each of the three sub-clocks
Steps back through the tempo modes, which are BPM CV and external sync at 24, 16, 12, 8, 4 or 2 pulses per step
Steps forward through the tempo modes, which are BPM CV and external sync at 2, 4, 8, 12, 16 or 24 pulses per step
Ratio of that clock to the master tempo: turned up it multiplies, turned down it divides, through whole numbers to 16 plus 1.5 and 2.5 and selected values on to 96; turning it shows that ratio
A trigger here restarts the time keeping of the master clock and all three sub-clocks
A trigger here toggles between run and pause; the menu can make this input follow a gate level instead

In CV mode this sets the tempo, with 0V giving 120 BPM and each volt doubling it. In a sync mode the clock locks to the pulses arriving here, and with nothing patched the tempo comes from the BPM knob
The master clock pulse, at the tempo set by the BPM knob or by the external clock
The pulse of that sub-clock, at its own ratio of the master tempo
A 10V pulse when the module is reset, for passing the reset on to sequencers or to another clock
A 10V pulse when run is switched on or off, for passing the run state on to sequencers or to another clock
Passes on the voltage at the BPM input when a cable is patched there; with nothing patched it gives the module's own tempo as a BPM CV
Menu — Outputs high on reset when not running holds the clock outputs high while a stopped clock is reset, so a sequential switch reset at that moment is not stepped on
Menu — On Start and On Stop each offer an internal reset and a reset pulse, so the clock and the sequencers it drives restart together
Menu — Run CV input is level sensitive makes the RUN input follow a gate rather than a trigger; in a chain of clocks only the first should have it turned on
Menu — Send triggers (instead of gates) switches any of the four clock outputs from a pulse with a width to a short trigger
Menu — Auto-patch makes this the clock master and patches the reset, run and BPM inputs of the other Clocked and Clkd modules to it, leaving already-patched inputs alone
Sixteen pads each holding a voltage, for calling up CV values by hand. They work as one group of sixteen, two of eight or four of four, and there are eight banks of stored values
Quantizes the main display and the CV outputs to the nearest semitone; the voltages stored in the pads are left as they are
Sets the voltage of the selected pad. It is set to high sensitivity so that the whole -10V to 10V range can be crossed quickly
Selects which of the eight banks of stored voltages is in use
Shows the main display in volts, or as a note name with sharps, or as a note name with flats
Divides the pads into four groups of four, two groups of eight or one group of sixteen. Each group has its own read head and its own pair of CV and gate outputs
With attach on, clicking a pad moves both the read head and the editing head; with it off only the editing head moves, so a pad can be changed without disturbing what is playing
Selects that pad: its stored voltage goes to the CV output of its group and appears on the main display
Moves on to the next pad after each write, so a run of voltages can be entered one after another from an external source
Stores the voltage present at the CV IN jack into the selected pad
Selects the bank from a voltage, 0-10V spread across the eight banks
A trigger here performs a write, so entry can be driven from a keyboard's gate output
The voltage that a write stores into the selected pad
The stored voltage of the pad selected in that group. Groups are taken in order, so in the 2x8 configuration the first and third of these jacks are used, and in 1x16 only the first; the rest give 0V
10V while a pad in that group is held down, and 0V throughout when attach is off; groups are taken in order, so 2x8 uses the first and third of these jacks and 1x16 only the first
Note — right-clicking the main CV display lets an exact voltage be typed for the selected pad
Menu — High sensitivity CV knob is on by default; turning it off makes the CV knob move in finer steps
Four-track phrase sequencer, 32 steps to a sequence, 64 sequences to a track and 99 phrases to a song, each track separately clocked and edited
Moves the edit head to that step, its lamps showing the gate and whether the step is picked out; while the length or repeat setting is open, clicking a step sets the length there and then
Extends every edit across a run of steps, as many of them as the 4/8/CUST switch chooses
Sets how many steps or phrases SEL and COPY-PASTE work on: four, eight, or a custom range picked out by clicking
Copies the current sequence, or the chosen part of it, into the buffer; in song mode it copies phrases instead
Writes the buffer into the current sequence from the edit head, or into the song in song mode
Switches the whole sequencer between editing and playing single sequences and building a song out of numbered phrases
Sets the octave of the step at the edit head; the lit button is the octave that step holds
Switches the keyboard between entering notes and entering gate types
Sets the value shown on the CV2 display for the step at the edit head: its second control voltage, its gate probability, or its slide time
Steps the CV2 display through the three things it can hold for a step: the second control voltage, the gate probability and the slide time
Chooses the sequence being played and edited, or in song mode the sequence number the current phrase calls up
Chooses which phrase of the song is being edited, in song mode only
Steps back through the four tracks, choosing the one every edit acts on
Steps forward through the four tracks, choosing the one every edit acts on
Applies every edit to all four tracks at once
Makes the edit heads follow the run heads, so the step being edited is the step being played
Starts and stops all four tracks; there is one run state for the whole module
Returns every track to the first step of its sequence or of its song
Opens transposing all 32 steps of the sequence or rotating the steps within its length, with the amount turned in on the sequence knob
Marks the current phrase as the first one the song plays, for working on one section of a long song
Marks the current phrase as the last one the song plays
Turns the gate of the step at the edit head on or off
Ties the step at the edit head to the step before it, so one note is held across both
Turns on probability for that step's gate, so the gate reaches the output only some of the time; the chance is set on the CV2 display, 0 to 1
Turns on portamento from the previous step's voltage into this one; the slide time is set on the CV2 display, 1 being a whole clock period
In sequence mode it sets how many steps the sequence plays; in song mode it sets how many times the current phrase repeats, 0 to 99, where 0 skips the phrase
Sets the order the steps are played in, or in song mode the order of the phrases: forward, reverse, ping-pong, pendulum, brownian, random, track A's positions, or each one once
Sets the track's clock resolution, which is what allows the advanced gate types, and its clock delay of 0 to 99 pulses; a reset is needed before a new delay takes effect
Moves the edit head on to the next step after each write, so a run of notes can be entered one after another
A trigger here writes whatever is arriving at the CV inputs into the step at the edit head; an input with no cable is left out of the write
The pitch written into that track's current step when a trigger reaches WRITE
Advances that track one step per pulse; with no cable patched, the track runs on the clock of the track before it
A trigger here starts and stops all four tracks
A trigger here returns every track to the first step of its sequence or of its song
The pitch of the step that track has reached, at a volt per octave
The gate of the step that track has reached
The second control voltage of the step that track has reached, 0-10V, for accents or velocity
Menu — Poly merge into track A outputs folds the CV, gate and CV2 of tracks B, C or D into track A's outputs as extra channels, and holds the merged tracks' own outputs at 0V
Menu — CV2 can be set in volts at 0.05V resolution, as numbered levels 0 to 127, or as semitones, and Bipolar changes its range from 0-10V to -5V to 5V
Expander for Foundry, placed immediately to the right of it; it adds CV inputs for the sequence, track, step and second control voltage, and a switch and a button of its own
Selects the sequence for that track; how the voltage is read is set by Seq CV in level in Foundry's menu
Selects the track, a 0-10V range mapped to A, B, C, D and then the same four again with any change applied across all tracks
Holds off a sequence change asked for at the SEQ# inputs until the end of the current sequence is reached
A trigger turns the gate of the step being edited on or off
A trigger turns the tie on the step being edited on or off
A trigger turns the slide on the step being edited on or off
A trigger turns gate probability on the step being edited on or off
A trigger moves one step to the left in SEQ mode, or one phrase back in SONG mode
A trigger moves one step to the right in SEQ mode, or one phrase forward in SONG mode
The CV2 value written into the current step of that track when a trigger arrives at Foundry's WRITE input
Chooses what a write records: the CV inputs only, the CV2 inputs only, or both
A trigger steps through what a write records: the CV inputs only, the CV2 inputs only, or both
Shows the note names of up to four voltages, or the name of the chord they spell, 8HP. Placed immediately to the right of ChordKey or CVPad it reads that module directly and needs no cables
Names each voltage as a note, or names the four together as a chord
A voltage to be named, read at 1V per octave
Passes on the voltage shown on that row, and gives 0V when nothing is feeding it
Menu — Allow poly in 1 to override fills all four displays from the channels of a polyphonic cable patched to input 1
Menu — Sharp, unchecked is flat, picks which spelling the note names use
Menu — the displayed notes can be copied in the Portable sequence format, for pasting as a chord in ChordKey or as a short sequence in a sequencer
Gate sequencer of 64 steps, each step carrying a probability, arranged as four rows of 16, two of 32 or one of 64, with a song mode of 64 phrases
Turns that step's gate on or off and moves the cursor to it; the step is green when its gate is on and yellow while its probability is open, and in song mode it picks a phrase instead
Chooses the shape of the gate for the step at the cursor; its lamp is green when the clock resolution can produce that shape and red when it cannot
Opens probability for the step at the cursor and puts it on the display, where the main knob sets it from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.02; pressing it again turns that step's probability off
Chooses the sequence being played and edited, or in song mode the sequence the phrase under the cursor calls up; it sets the probability instead while one is on the display
Switches between editing one sequence and building a song out of 64 phrases
Sets the length of the sequence and its run mode; held for 2 seconds it opens the clock resolution in pulses per step, which is what unlocks the gate types
Splits the 64 steps into four sequences of 16, two of 32, or one of 64
Starts and stops the sequencer
Returns the sequencer to its first step, and puts the write cursor back at the first step
Copies the current sequence, or as much of it as the 4/8/ALL switch chooses, into the buffer; in song mode it copies phrases
Writes the buffer into the current sequence from the cursor, or into the song in song mode
Sets how much copy and paste carry: four steps, eight steps, or the whole sequence together with its length and run mode
Advances the sequencer one step per pulse; with a clock resolution above one it takes that many pulses for each step
A trigger here returns the sequencer to its first step
A trigger here starts and stops the sequencer
Chooses the sequence from a voltage
The gates of one of the sequences; with four rows of 16 each output carries a row, with two of 32 the first and third carry them, and with one of 64 only the first
Menu — the display can be locked so that steps, gate types and the probability button cannot be changed by accident
Note — pressing copy in one mode and paste in the other runs a shortcut instead: randomizing the gates or the probabilities, clearing the sequence, or refilling the song
Expander for GateSeq64, placed immediately to the right of it; it adds CV inputs for writing gates and probabilities into the sequencer, and works in sequence mode only
A trigger here writes the gate and probability arriving at the other inputs into the step under the cursor and moves the cursor on; with neither of those patched it only moves the cursor on
Sets the gate state written into the step, so a pattern can be entered from another module
Sets the probability written into the step
A trigger here writes an on-gate into the step under the cursor and moves the cursor on
A trigger here writes an off-gate into the step under the cursor and moves the cursor on
A trigger here moves the cursor back one step
Sends a trigger when a chosen keyboard key is pressed, 3HP; the mouse cursor must be over the module for the key to register
Press it, then press a key to store that key, with any modifiers held, as the hotkey. The light shows red until the key is taken
Holds the trigger back after the key is pressed, 0 to 1 second
A 10V pulse lasting 2ms each time the hotkey is pressed
Menu — Treat modifiers as key hits allows shift, control, alt or the command key to be stored as the hotkey in its own right; the menu also shows which key is currently stored
Four-tap delay for note events rather than audio, carrying pitch, gate and a second CV for velocity or panning; each tap comes back as extra channels of the polyphonic outputs
Sets the delay of that tap in tempo steps, up to 32; at 0 the tap is switched off
Transposes the pitch of that tap by a number of semitones, -48 to 48
Adds a random semitone offset to the pitch of that tap; turned right the offset is bipolar and turned left it is unipolar, as far as two octaves either way
Sets the probability that the gate of that tap fires
Offsets or scales the CV2 output of that tap: an offset of minus 10V to 10V, or a scaling of minus 1 to 1, according to the CV2 mode switch
Sets the polyphony of the CV, GATE and CV2 inputs, 1 to 4. At 4, one tap must be switched off or WET ONLY turned on, to keep the total inside 16 channels
The voltage the CV2 input takes when nothing is patched to it, -10V to 10V
In the chord setting one probability draw covers every channel of a tap, so its notes play all or none; in the separate setting each channel is drawn on its own
Picks whether the CV2 knobs offset the CV2 output or scale it
Picks whether the TEMPO input takes clock pulses or a BPM-CV
Leaves the undelayed tap out of the outputs, so only the delay taps are heard
Pitch in, sampled and held on the rising edge of the gate on the matching channel
Gates marking the notes to be delayed; each rising edge samples the CV and CV2 inputs
A second CV, for velocity or panning, sampled and held on the rising edge of the matching gate
A trigger here erases the delay tape
Clock setting the speed of the delay tape, so the delay knobs count its steps
Pitch of every tap, one polyphonic channel per tap for each input channel
Gate of every tap, on the channels matching the CV output
CV2 of every tap, on the channels matching the CV output
Menu — tempo multiplier runs the delay tape at a multiple or a fraction of the clock at the TEMPO input
Menu — low CPU mode refreshes the outputs less often; it does not change how the inputs are processed
Drops a note from a polyphonic note stream when another channel is already sounding the same pitch, and can delay the gate input by a few samples
Delays the gate input by 0 to 5 samples, for when the CV from an upstream module arrives later than its gate
Pitch in, sampled on each rising gate on the matching channel
Gates marking the notes; the number of channels here sets the polyphony of all three outputs
A second CV, for velocity or panning, sampled on each rising gate on the matching channel
Pitch of the notes that were kept
Gate of each note that was kept; a note whose pitch matches one already sounding on another channel produces no gate
CV2 of the notes that were kept
Note — the inputs are sampled and held on the gates, so modulation that moves between gates does not pass through
Looper for note events rather than audio, carrying pitch, gate and a second CV for velocity or panning, up to 16 channels
Sets the length of the loop in tempo steps, 1 to 32
Erases the tape
Turns looping on: the tape is read back at the point set by LENGTH and written to its own input, and the CV, GATE and CV2 inputs are ignored. Tempo and length changes have no effect while it runs
Picks whether the TEMPO input takes clock pulses or a BPM-CV
A trigger here erases the tape
A trigger here toggles looping
Clock setting the speed of the tape, so the length knob counts its steps
Pitch in, sampled and held on the rising edge of the gate on the matching channel
Gates marking the notes to be recorded; each rising edge samples the CV and CV2 inputs
A second CV, for velocity or panning, sampled and held on the rising edge of the matching gate
Pitch of the recorded or looped notes
Gate of the recorded or looped notes
CV2 of the recorded or looped notes
Menu — tempo multiplier runs the tape at a multiple or a fraction of the clock at the TEMPO input
Menu — CV2 normalization sets the voltage the CV2 input takes when nothing is patched to it
Note — the tape is not saved with the patch, and looping is off whenever a patch is loaded
Gate splitter, 6HP: each gate goes to one of two outputs according to whether its pitch is above or below a split point, channel by channel on a polyphonic cable
Shows the split point on the display as a voltage or as a note name
Sets the split point, -10V to 10V
The pitch that each gate is judged by, at 1V per octave; on a polyphonic cable each channel is compared with the split point separately
The gates to be split; each channel goes to one output or the other according to the pitch on the matching channel of the CV input
